PullRequest.Title: mcp: don't expand .mcp.json URLs that the Copilot runtime rejects
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #340369. Part of #340161.

#340369 expands `${VAR}` anywhere in a workspace `.mcp.json` server's URL. The Copilot runtime is stricter: it parses the URL as written, before expanding it, and rejects the server if it doesn't parse. As a result, some URLs now work in VS Code's own chat while the same server is rejected in Copilot sessions, which goes beyond what migration needs.

## Changes

A URL is now expanded only if it parses as a URL (`URL.canParse`). Otherwise it's left unexpanded, as it was before #340369.

| URL in `.mcp.json` | Copilot runtime | VS Code after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Host, path, query: `https://${HOST}/mcp?key=${KEY}` | ✅ | ✅ expanded |
| Default in path or query: `/${R:-eu}/mcp?k=${K:-x}` | ✅ | ✅ expanded |
| Default in the host: `https://${HOST:-example.com}/mcp` | ❌ rejected | Left as written (was expanded) |
| Port: `http://localhost:${PORT}/mcp` | ❌ rejected | Left as written (was expanded) |
| Whole URL: `${BASE}/mcp` | ❌ rejected | Left as written (was expanded) |

Header values are still expanded even when the URL isn't.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Source for the Copilot behaviour:** `.mcp.json` servers go through `workspace_discovery.rs` → `parse_workspace_config` → `validate_server_config` → `validate_remote_server`, which calls `Url::parse` on the URL as written and drops the server with "url: Invalid url". I checked each URL form by running the runtime's `url` crate (2.5.8, toolchain 1.98.1). `URL.canParse` follows the same WHATWG standard and gave the same result for every form.
- **Not changed:** a URL whose scheme is a variable (`${SCHEME}://...`) still makes VS Code drop every server in that `.mcp.json`, because `URI.parse` throws in `claudeConfigToServerDefinition`. That predates #340369.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/mcp/test/common/envVarResolution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/mcpEnvironmentVariableExpansion.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/workspaceDotMcpDiscovery.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/mcpRegistry.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadMcp.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/mcpServerConnection.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/mcpServerRequestHandler.test.ts`: 169 passing, 14 pending (from an existing `.skip`)
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: clean

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a migrated workspace HTTP MCP server whose raw URL contains a supported environment reference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: McpServer.start serializes one connection attempt, resolveConnection checks the raw URL, then the extension host expands it before the HTTP transport starts. The added URL.canParse checks are on this startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the launch to the extension host, expand environment references using the host process environment, and deserialize the result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC round trip per server-start attempt that has a recognized URL or header reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one IPC round trip occurred for a parseable raw URL containing a recognized reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC must finish before the remote HTTP connection can be created.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the existing HTTP/SSE MCP transport to the resolved remote server URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport start per resolved server connection, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote transport was started after environment expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The server cannot become connected until the remote transport starts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One raw URL per server-start attempt; supported expansion is already limited to URLs of at most 1,000 UTF-16 code units by hasEnvVarReferences. Retries repeat the check, while starts for different servers remain independent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Starts are serialized per McpServer by _connectionSequencer; there is no new aggregate limiter or new concurrency introduced by the diff. Different servers may start concurrently as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in URL validation or expansion. Warm and cold starts both perform the checks once per attempted connection; the diff neither defeats nor adds a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path shows URL.canParse once in the main-thread precheck and once in extension-host expansion, with the existing IPC and network boundaries unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact URL parsing cost varies by JavaScript runtime, but expandable inputs are capped at 1,000 code units and server starts are not a per-frame or per-message path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds two bounded URL parses on starts that still expand, but does not increase IPC/network cardinality or create realistic latency, throughput, or memory impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a migrated workspace HTTP MCP server whose raw URL is rejected by URL.canParse
Scenarios.CriticalPath: resolveConnection calls URL.canParse before deciding whether environment expansion is needed. With no expandable header, a rejected raw URL now avoids the extension-host expansion IPC; with an expandable header, the existing IPC still occurs so the header can be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Expand host environment references when any supported header reference remains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero IPC calls for an invalid raw URL with no expandable headers, versus one before the diff; one IPC if headers require expansion, unchanged from before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, a recognized reference in the invalid raw URL caused one expansion IPC even without header references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When present, IPC remains on the startup critical path; when absent, the diff shortens that path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt to create the remote MCP HTTP transport from the launch URI retained by connection resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one transport start per connection attempt, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connection resolution also proceeded to one transport start after expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transport startup remains necessary for the server to connect; the diff changes URL expansion semantics but does not fan out network operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One URL check per server-start attempt. Cost grows linearly with the configured URL length; ordinary MCP URLs are small, and the changed work is not inside a collection or message loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-server attempts remain serialized; rejected URLs do not create new concurrent work and can remove one IPC from an attempt without expandable headers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no positive or negative validation cache. Each retry rechecks the raw URL, but retries already repeated connection resolution and the check is one local parse per attempt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the short-circuit behavior and optional IPC are explicit in getExpandableUrl and launchHasEnvironmentVariableReferences.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extremely large configuration strings could make URL.canParse more expensive, but such inputs are not a realistic MCP URL workload and configuration parsing already processes the same string. There is no evidenced user-visible performance symptom.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The main changed boundary effect is eliminating an IPC for rejected URL-only references; remaining synchronous parsing is once per attempt and not a realistic regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a migrated workspace HTTP MCP server with a plain URL and no environment references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: resolveConnection now runs URL.canParse and then the existing reference scan; it does not call the extension host and proceeds to the existing remote transport.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Environment expansion IPC is skipped because no supported references are present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reference scan returned false and skipped expansion IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No IPC is added to startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the remote MCP HTTP transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per connection attempt before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transport was started directly after reference detection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing network operation dominates connection establishment and is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One URL per server-start attempt; for normal configurations this is a short string. The added parser is not invoked per tool call, protocol message, render, or frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-server start sequencing is unchanged. Different server starts may overlap as before, but each contributes only one local parse and no added IPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used; both first starts and retries perform one parse. The diff does not alter server metadata or connection caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper is called exactly once by launchHasEnvironmentVariableReferences on this main-thread path and short-circuits the extension-host call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark quantifies URL.canParse, but the operation is one local parse of a normal configuration URL per connection attempt, so plausible impact is negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds minor synchronous CPU work but no meaningful hot-path multiplicity, retained state, boundary fan-out, or user-visible performance consequence.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced MCP discovery, connection resolution, extension-host expansion IPC, per-server sequencing, and remote transport startup. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; no findings or regression-fix records were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
